questions.prompt: What is wrong with the Winlogon Userinit value in this export?
options: It is missing the trailing comma
A second path is appended after the comma, and Windows runs every comma-separated entry at every logon
It points to the wrong system directory
It should be set to explorer.exe
questions.explanation: The correct value is exactly C:\Windows\system32\userinit.exe, with nothing after it. Note also that Shell is untouched, so checking only Shell would miss this.

questions.prompt: Why is the IFEO Debugger on sethc.exe particularly serious?
options: Sticky Keys is reachable from the lock screen before authentication, so it yields a SYSTEM shell with no credentials at all
It prevents the system from booting
questions.explanation: On an RDP-reachable host this is a standing remote backdoor that survives credential resets entirely, because it requires no credentials to use.

questions.prompt: The WinDefendUpdate service has Type=0x10. What does that tell you?
options: It is a kernel driver, indicating BYOVD
It is an own-process service rather than a driver, so this is ordinary service persistence
It is disabled and can be ignored
It runs only in safe mode
questions.explanation: Type 1 would indicate a kernel driver and a different threat model. Type 16 (0x10) is a standard own-process service.

questions.prompt: Why does removing one of these four mechanisms not clean the host?
options: Registry changes cannot be removed without a reboot
Redundant persistence is the norm in real intrusions -- each survives independently, and the IFEO backdoor survives even a full credential reset
The registry export is only a partial snapshot
Windows automatically restores deleted Run keys
questions.explanation: Declaring a host clean after removing a single mechanism is how reinfection happens, which is why the correlation step across all persistence locations matters.
